releaseName: Faster, tidier career interview in your language
summary: Live interview replies come sooner: a short spoken acknowledgement plays while the interviewer writes, and the question plays sentence by sentence as its audio arrives (#2409). Each turn logs how long recognition, the interviewer and the voice took, with no words or audio. Talk live opens on the signed-in screen too (#2393). The interview gains an End this conversation button, profile facts for subjects the candidate types, numbered topic cards, clearer topic reasons and name hints for live recognition (#2414). Career evidence files show when each was added and can be downloaded; a quarantined file downloads only for owners and admins (#2413). A new screen language applies without a refresh (#2412). The career interview speaks the screen's language throughout: topic reasons and the opening offer are worded on the screen, the interviewer's fixed sentences follow the conversation's language, and a confirmed topic's evidence file has French headings and labels on a French screen (#2418 to #2420). Coding agents get their own section in Workspace settings: it creates an agent token with the scopes you tick and gives a ready-to-copy setup for the Claude Code plugin, Claude Code, Codex and other MCP agents (#2427, #2439). With those scopes, an agent lists your job applications, adds a job from pasted text and follows a CV run; approvals stay in DraftLoop (#2438, #2440). DraftLoop installs as a Claude Code plugin from its repository, with the /log-work and /tailor-cv skills (#2441).
knownLimitations: The interviewer's question is still written in one call before it is spoken; streaming it into the voice waits on the turn timings. French is beta until the French quality gate (milestone 83) runs. The screening shadow only logs. Live speech and the career interview still need DRAFT_LOOP_SCREENING=rules+model and a Claude key on staging. Topics saved before this release show a neutral sentence instead of their full reason, and evidence files already confirmed stay in English. The local-first desktop has no career interview.
